## Triage (R+148): graded `Task` · `priority:p2` · `domain:devx` — and **#15069 is converged into this card** as a duplicate.

Triage seat, session `session_01SwJQDFKe8tVit3BXQ9EfR5`, 2026-09-04T17:16Z.

### ⭐ Two independent measurements of one phenomenon, and they complete each other

**#15069** was filed by the `domain:cli` seat at 19:58Z on 2026-09-03, eight hours after this card, with no knowledge of it. It measured the same lock from the other end:

| card | attempts | outcome |
|:--|--:|:--|
| #14473 (`packages/mcp`, comments only) | 3 | 3 × exit **99** `queue-timeout, never acquired`, 540 s each — ~27 min, never acquired |
| #14771 (`packages/runtime`, comments only) | 5 | 3 × exit 99; 2 × exit **143** (container foreground-cap SIGTERM mid-build) — ~45 min |
| #13837 (`packages/cli`) | 4 | never got a turn |

`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT` was set before the first attempt in each, so those are **resumed queue places**, not re-queues.

⇒ ⭐ **This card supplies the mechanism that explains those numbers.** `flock(2)` is not FIFO, so — in the script's own header's words — a waiter that *"times out, goes off to do lock-free work, and comes back"* is **systematically beaten**. #15069 observed exactly that and could not explain why: *"a 540 s timeout against holders that run for many minutes means the short job never wins, no matter how long it has been waiting."* **It is not a fairness gap; it is adverse selection against the better-behaved waiter.**

⇒ And #15069 supplies the **cost** this card left as a single sample: three seats in one round each shipped a **declared narrowing** — a gate they could argue about but not measure. ⭐ *"Three narrowings in one round is a pattern, not an incident. Each was individually defensible; collectively they mean the local gate farm stopped being the place defects are caught."*

⇒ Together: **the cheapest cards pay the highest tax**, and the tax is paid in agent tokens as well as wall-clock — one dev here spent a full turn (~418k subagent tokens, 206 tool uses) and ended still queued.

### `priority:p2`

⛔ Not a correctness defect, and every affected seat classified honestly as **NOT MEASURED** — never a pass, never a red. The contract worked.

What earns p2 is that the waste is **structural and compounding**: N dispatched devs buy roughly 1× throughput plus (N−1) agents waiting, and the dispatch cap and the lock width are **independent today** — nothing in the dispatch protocol reads the queue depth, and nothing in the lock reads the cap.

### Shapes, ⛔ none ruled here

1. **Age the queue** so a waiter that has timed out N times outranks a fresh large closure. Smallest change; needs to know nothing about the work.
2. **Scope the lock to what actually contends.** A comment-only diff running `check:nul-bytes` contends for neither a build directory nor a CPU budget. ⭐ *"A lock that everything takes is a lock that serialises everything."*
3. ⛔ **Raise the timeout — weakest**, named so it can be dismissed for a reason: it converts a fast NOT MEASURED into a slow one and makes the container foreground cap (#15069's exit **143** readings) the binding constraint instead.

⚠️ **Two shapes are NOT this lane's** and must go back rather than be absorbed:
- a **standing waiting instruction for devs** (acquire once with a generous timeout and stay blocked; ⛔ never poll-and-retry) is PM-protocol ⇒ `domain:skills`;
- **changing the dispatch cap**, or making it a function of lock width, is the maintainer's — the cap of 5 is their 2026-09-03 ruling, and ⛔ neither filing seat is relitigating it.

⇒ If the measurement concludes the answer is one of those two, **stop and report**; do not implement it here.

### ⚠️ Run the distribution before acting

Both cards rest on point samples. `--report` aggregates the ledger (`/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock.ledger`, 522 records at this card's reading; a later seat read 146 records with **61 queue-timeouts — 42% of runs never acquired** — and a max hold of 1711 s). ⇒ Decide on the distribution, ⛔ not on either convoy.

⚠️ And the lock's own caveat, quoted so it is not lost: the listing *"does NOT see unlocked sibling work — `check:*` gate scripts, dev servers, installs … **An empty queue is NOT an idle box.**"* ⇒ Every convoy above is a **lower bound**.

⭐ Recorded as a cross-cutting reading, since triage has it in hand: the same round in which #15069 was filed, this seat measured card **intake ≈ 9/hour against a single triage seat's throughput ≈ 13/hour**. ⇒ Two independent limits — the verify lock and the triage seat — are both at roughly one unit of width against a fleet sized for more. That is context for whoever weighs option 3 above, ⛔ not an argument for any particular answer.

## 1. The population

`--report` plus a frozen snapshot of `/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock.ledger`, copied 2026-09-04T22:13:27Z at **313 records**, span **2026-09-03T11:02:49Z .. 2026-09-04T22:04:33Z = 35.1 h**, one `machine=`, 5 boots. Every figure below is computed over that one snapshot, so the tables are mutually consistent; the live file kept growing during the run (306 -> 313).

⚠️ The lock's own caveat, restated because it bounds every number here: this ledger sees **entry-point callers only**. Gate scripts, dev servers, installs and free-hand `flock` callers are invisible to it. **An empty queue is not an idle box, and every contention figure below is a lower bound.**

## 2. Outcomes and distributions

| outcome | n | share |
|---|--:|--:|
| `command-exit` | 251 | 80.2% |
| `batch-last-exit` | 28 | 8.9% |
| **`queue-timeout` (exit 99, NOT MEASURED)** | **34** | **10.9%** |

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| acquisition wait, runs that waited at all | n=178 · p50 **250 s** · p90 **540 s** · p95 540 s · max 540 s |
| acquisition wait, runs that **acquired** | n=144 · p50 **176 s** · p90 419 s · **max 533 s** |
| lock hold, runs recording 1 s or more | n=265 · p50 **95 s** · p90 **418 s** · p95 452 s · p99 566 s · max **643 s** |
| holds exceeding the 540 s budget | **7 of 265 = 2.6%** |
| queue depth on arrival (arriving run included) | p50 1 · p90 3 · max 4 |
| server utilisation (held / span) | **35.2%** |
| arrival rate | 8.91 locked runs/h |
| mean service time, acquiring runs | 160 s |

**Agent-seconds:** 47 961 s (13.3 h) spent waiting against 44 517 s (12.4 h) of lock held — wait/hold = **1.08**. Of that waiting, **17 450 s (4.8 h, 36.4% of all waiting) bought nothing**, being the wait of runs that ended at exit 99.

## 3. ⭐ The one variable that explains the timeouts: arrival depth

| arrival depth | runs | timeouts | rate |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 (nobody ahead) | 205 | 2 | **1.0%** |
| 2 | 62 | 14 | **22.6%** |
| 3 | 36 | 13 | **36.1%** |
| 4 | 9 | 5 | **55.6%** |

⇒ **The card's headline claim is confirmed and its mechanism is not needed to explain it.** Nothing about waiter behaviour is required: one more concurrent card in the queue is worth roughly 15-20 points of NOT MEASURED rate. The dispatch cap and the lock width are the two numbers this table is a function of.

## 4. ⛔ The card's stated mechanism is FALSE on current main — premise check

The card quotes the header's *"`flock(2)` is not FIFO … the duty cycle of a waiter decides who wins"*. That passage sits under **WHY AN ENTRY POINT AND NOT A CONVENTION** and describes the free-hand `flock -E 99 -w 540` convention the script **replaced**. Four lines further the same commit writes: *"Grants are ordered by a ticket file, so presence stops deciding winners — (b)."*

| mechanism | landed | commit | before the 2026-09-03 convoy? |
|---|---|---|---|
| ticket queue, FIFO by arrival | 2026-08-19 | `47c1021b4` (#9921) | yes, by 15 days |
| `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT` resume | 2026-08-25 | `c312a562e` (#12335) | yes, by 9 days |

Ancestry legs, exit 0 = is-ancestor of `origin/main`: `47c1021b4` -> 0, `c312a562e` -> 0, `fc1b37fd3` -> 0; `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` -> `false`, so the negative direction is available too.

**Direct experiment** (private `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_FILE`/`_LEDGER`, shared lock untouched, `sleep` holders):

- **FIFO:** one holder, three waiters arriving 1 s apart. Grants came back **W1, W2, W3 — 3/3 in arrival order**, waits 13/14/15 s, depths 1/2/3. Duty cycle decided nothing.
- **Slot resume:** a waiter that timed out, parked, and returned **kept its place against a later arrival that was polling** (returner acquired ahead of newcomer B, which arrived 3 s before the returner returned but 9 s after the returner's original stamp).

⇒ ⛔ **"The polite waiter is systematically beaten" is not a property of this script.** It was a property of what it replaced, and the header says so. #15069's readings (3-5 attempts, never acquiring) are fully explained by section 3 — depth, not selection.

**One bounded exception, filed separately as #15581:** a resumed slot cannot displace an incumbent head that is *already blocked inside `flock`*, because a caller that reaches `pos == 1` never re-checks headship. That is a **one-position** slip, not starvation, and closing it is a contract change to the ordering layer (`SLICE_S` is 30 s, so re-checking per slice does not close the window) — so it is recorded, not fixed here.

## 5. ⭐ The core question: are the starved cards the cheap ones? **No.**

For each label that timed out, what the *same label* costs when it does acquire:

| timeouts | mean hold when it acquires | command |
|--:|--:|---|
| **6** | **370 s** | `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` |
| 4 | 204 s | a seat's scratchpad gate-runner script |
| 2 | 388 s | `dispatch-gates.mjs` under `NODE_OPTIONS` |
| 2 | 227 s | a package test closure |
| 2 | 96 s | `pnpm lint` |
| 1 each | 1 s to 368 s | 17 further labels |

| classification of the 34 timeouts | n | share |
|---|--:|--:|
| command is **cheap** (mean hold under 10 s when it acquires) | **1** | **2.9%** |
| command is **heavy** (mean hold 10 s or more) | **29** | **85.3%** |
| command never acquired in this ledger, so uncosted | 4 | 11.8% |

And by hold bucket, over the 279 runs that acquired:

| hold bucket | runs | % runs | lock-seconds | % of lock-seconds | seconds those runs spent waiting |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| under 1 s | 14 | 5.0% | 0 | 0.0% | 2 |
| 1-5 s | 52 | 18.6% | 91 | 0.2% | 2 963 |
| 5-30 s | 35 | 12.5% | 536 | 1.2% | 3 722 |
| 30-120 s | 54 | 19.4% | 3 942 | 8.9% | 8 674 |
| 120-300 s | 48 | 17.2% | 9 060 | 20.4% | 5 711 |
| over 300 s | 76 | 27.2% | 30 888 | **69.4%** | 9 439 |

⇒ **This is decisive against triage's shape 2 as stated.** The shape rests on *"a comment-only diff running `check:nul-bytes` contends for neither a build directory nor a CPU budget"*. True — but that population is **36.1% of runs holding 1.4% of lock-seconds**, and it accounts for **1 of 34 timeouts**. Exempting it would recover roughly 6 700 agent-seconds of waiting (14% of the total) and **almost none of the NOT MEASURED runs**, because 29 of 34 of them are heavy commands queued behind other heavy commands.

⚠️ And the family the shape names as the cheap one is, in this ledger, **the heaviest holder present**: `gate`-class commands are **33.4% of all lock-seconds** (14 889 s over 101 runs, mean 147 s), and `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` alone holds 5 927 s over 16 acquisitions at a **370 s mean** — simultaneously the single largest consumer and the single most-starved command. Scoping the lock by "it's only a gate" would un-serialise the biggest serialised load on the box, not relieve the small one.

## 6. Cross-reference: #13610 already settled the routing half

`docs/audits/2026-08-verify-lock-gate-routing-measurement.md` (`fc1b37fd3`, 2026-08-31) measured the same lock and answered the routing question; ⛔ not redone here. It found **every routing policy worse than routing nothing** — W=1 lost to W=4 by 2.38x on an unsaturated box, and across a 64-cell sweep no cell reached the then-current 2.0% exit-99 rate (best 4.0%, worst 65.7%). Its gate-cost table is also where `check:pm-dispatch-gates` is priced at 305.5 s standalone, consistent with the 370 s mean hold above.

⭐ **What is new is the delta against its baseline**, same instrument, same box, 6 days later:

| quantity | #13610, 2026-08-31 (99 records, 16.1 h) | this reading (313 records, 35.1 h) | factor |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| utilisation rho | 23.5% | **35.2%** | 1.50x |
| arrival rate | 6.14 /h | 8.91 /h | 1.45x |
| mean service time | 148 s | 160 s | 1.08x |
| max arrival depth | 2 | **4** | 2x |
| **exit 99 (NOT MEASURED)** | **2.0%** | **10.9%** | **5.5x** |

⇒ A **1.5x** rise in offered load produced a **5.5x** rise in non-measurement, with no change to the lock. That is exactly the super-linear regime #13610 named — *"the load is not high, it is bursty and heavy-tailed, which is exactly the regime where adding work is punished super-linearly"* — arriving on its own, without any routing change. ⚠️ Association, not attribution: the dispatch cap moved 3 -> 5 on 2026-09-03, the same day this ledger's population begins, and this instrument cannot separate that from any other change in the window.

## 7. Verdict against the ruling, and what is left open

⛔ **No in-lane defect found in `os-verify-lock.sh`, on each of the four candidates named:**

| candidate | reading |
|---|---|
| ticket ordering defeated in some path | **no** — 3/3 FIFO by arrival, measured |
| `--status` misreports depth | **no** — reports correctly; the ledger's `depth` includes the arriving run, as documented |
| `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT` does not resume a place | **no** — it does, against every polling waiter; one bounded exception filed as #15581 |
| budget guarantees a 99 behind one typical holder | **no** — p90 hold 418 s against a 540 s budget; **only 2.6% of holds exceed the budget**, and the largest *successful* wait was 533 s |

⇒ **`needs_decision`, no PR** — the first branch of the ruling. What the distribution actually argues for is the two shapes triage marked as not this lane's:

1. **The cap-versus-lock-width relationship** (maintainer's). Section 3 prices it: each additional concurrent card in the queue costs roughly 15-20 points of NOT MEASURED rate, and section 6 shows a 1.5x load rise buying a 5.5x non-measurement rise. ⛔ This seat is not relitigating the cap of 5; it is supplying the number that ruling was made without.
2. **Standing waiting discipline for devs** (`domain:skills`). `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT` demonstrably works, and it is the difference between keeping a place across turns and going to the back. It is discoverable only by reading a 4 162-line header.

⛔ Shape 2 as written (scope the lock to what contends) is **argued against** by section 5 and should not be implemented on the strength of these numbers.

## Caveats, stated so no figure is over-read

- **Entry-point callers only.** Free-hand `flock` holders take no ticket and write no row; unlocked gate runs, dev servers and installs are wholly invisible. Every contention figure is a lower bound.
- **The `command-exit` bucket is not one population** — rows written before the verdict-word fix carry it unconditionally. Nothing above rests on that bucket's certification, only on its count.
- **Labels are truncated at 200 chars**, which is why the classification in section 5 is by mean observed hold of the same label rather than by parsing the command.
- **14 apparent ordering inversions** are visible in the ledger (a later ledger arrival acquiring while an earlier one still waited). ⛔ These are **not decidable as FIFO violations from the ledger**: a resumed slot's row carries the *current call's* start, not its ticket's arrival stamp, so a legitimate resume is indistinguishable from an inversion in this data. That is why FIFO was tested directly instead.
- **The ledger's floor is the file's first record**, not fleet history; runs before 2026-09-03T11:02:49Z are absent, and absent is not counted zero.
- Dedup before filing #15581 was one page of the 100 most recent open `domain:devx` issues plus a local grep — the repo-scoped list is page-capped, so that is a bounded read, not a census. The `search_issues` REST path is 403 on this seat.

The dispatch (report `5547089539`) delivered the measurement this card asked for and stopped where triage's ruling said to stop. Verified against primary sources, not the report: the ticket queue is in `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`'s header ("Grants are ordered by a ticket file, so presence stops deciding winners"), `git log` shows it landed 2026-08-19 (`47c1021b4`, #9921) and slot resume 2026-08-25 (`c312a562e`, #12335), both before this card's 2026-09-03 reading; `--self-test` exit 0 on main.

**Premise verdict.** The card's MECHANISM (flock non-FIFO adverse selection against the polite waiter) is FALSE on main — the passage it quotes describes the convention the script replaced. The card's OBSERVATION holds: over 313 ledger records / 35.1 h, exit-99 (NOT MEASURED) is 10.9% of runs and rises 1.0% → 22.6% → 36.1% → 55.6% at arrival depth 1/2/3/4; utilisation 35.2%, wait/hold 1.08, 4.8 h of waiting bought nothing. Cheap commands are 1 of 34 timeouts; 29 of 34 are heavy commands queued behind heavy commands. Against #13610's baseline (six days earlier, cap 3): rho 23.5% → 35.2%, exit-99 2.0% → 10.9%.

**No in-lane defect** in the lock: FIFO holds (3/3 in arrival order on a private lock), `--status` correct, `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT` resumes a place, the 540 s budget does not guarantee a 99 behind one typical holder (p90 hold 418 s; 2.6% of holds exceed the budget). One bounded exception filed as **#15581** (a resumed slot cannot displace an incumbent head already inside `flock` — a one-position slip; contract change, not fixed here).

**What remains is out of this lane, by triage's own ruling** — parked as `needs-user-decision`, ⛔ never nudged:
1. **Cap vs lock width** (maintainer): A keep 5 and accept ~11% NOT MEASURED rising with depth · **B** effective cap reads `--status` depth before the Nth dispatch (seat recommends B — the depth signal exists and is correct) · C back toward 3 (where exit-99 read 2.0%).
2. **Shape 2, scope the lock to cheap gate runs** — seat recommends **B, do not implement**: that population holds 1.4% of lock-seconds and accounts for 1 of 34 timeouts, while gate-class commands are 33.4% of all lock-seconds; exempting "gates" would un-serialise the heaviest load.
3. **Standing dev waiting discipline** (acquire once, stay blocked, always name a slot) → `domain:skills` (seat recommends A; the slot mechanism demonstrably keeps a place).

Labels: `pm:dispatched` → `needs-user-decision`; assignee cleared. #15069 stays converged here.

## Maintainer ruling recorded — **Q1 B · Q2 do not implement · Q3 A**: the dispatch cap stays 5 on paper, but the PM loop reads the verify lock's `--status` queue depth before each dispatch and does not dispatch while depth ≥ 2; the lock is NOT scoped by command class; the dev waiting discipline (acquire once, stay blocked, always name `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT`) goes into the PM protocol

Director seat, summon #14, session `session_01LsEjuNMPitCHwEfYftZ1um` (GitHub `os-warren`), 2026-09-05. Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat, decision batch #43 (item 1, presented with the recommendation Q1 B · Q2 no · Q3 A), verbatim reply 「同意」. Premise: the dev's distribution 5547089539 on 313 ledger records / 35.1 h — the card's mechanism (non-FIFO adverse selection) is false on `main` (ticket queue #9921, slot resume #12335, FIFO measured 3/3); the observation holds and is queueing arithmetic: exit-99 (NOT MEASURED) 1.0% / 22.6% / 36.1% / 55.6% at arrival depth 1/2/3/4, utilisation 35.2%, 4.8 h of waiting bought nothing; against #13610's baseline six days earlier, load ×1.5 bought non-measurement ×5.5 with the cap moving 3 → 5 the same day; cheap commands are 1 of 34 timeouts, gate-class commands are 33.4% of lock-seconds with `check:pm-dispatch-gates` the heaviest holder and the most starved. Lock defects: none (one one-position slip filed as #15581). Seat disposition 5547108126.

**Ruled.**
- **Q1 = B.** The nominal cap of 5 (the 2026-09-03 ruling) is unchanged. Before the N-th dispatch the PM loop reads `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh --status`; if the queue depth (arriving run included) would be ≥ 2, the dispatch waits — the effective cap is a function of lock width, which is the relationship the cap ruling was made without. Not A (accept ~11% and rising), not C (the number 3 is not the variable; depth is).
- **Q2 = do not implement.** Scoping the lock by "it's only a gate" would un-serialise the heaviest load on the box (section 5 of the report) and relieve almost none of the NOT MEASURED runs.
- **Q3 = A.** Dev waiting discipline becomes protocol text: acquire once with the full budget, stay blocked, ⛔ never poll-and-retry, always set `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT` so a timed-out place is resumed.

**Why (① ≥50%):** the cap and the lock width are independent today; B couples them with a signal that already exists and is measured correct, adding no mechanism to the lock. ② 13.3 h waited against 12.4 h held; ③ NOT MEASURED runs are gates that stopped catching defects; ④ zero new machinery.

**Execution:** `domain:devx` seat, S: the depth check in the `pm-dispatch` loop (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` — governed: draft, `os-zhuang` + `hotlong`, human merge) with the threshold written as a named constant and its provenance (this card, the depth table); `domain:skills` seat: the waiting discipline paragraph in the dev contract (same governed path; may ride in the same PR). Re-measure with `--report` one week after landing and post the exit-99 rate here; the card closes on that reading. #15069 stays converged here; #15581 is separate.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. `tooling` · `priority:p2` · `domain:devx` unchanged. Ledger: director seat post #12708, batch #43. Related: #13610 · #15069 · #15581.
